extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent attorneys, and other patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpt from the MPEP and related AIA statutory provisions covering (a) procedural review rules for covered business method patent litigation, (b) the definition and scope of "covered business method patent," (c) an ATM venue exemption, and (d) a statutory ban on patents directed to human organisms. Also includes the MPEP index listing many patent-law topics and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory appeal and Federal Circuit review (covered business method transitional proceeding)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may take an immediate interlocutory appeal from a district court’s decision under paragraph (1). The United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit shall review the district court’s decision to ensure consistent application of established precedent, and such review may be de novo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rule governing appeals in the transitional proceeding for covered business method patents: interlocutory appeals are permitted and the Federal Circuit may review de novo to promote consistent application of precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: ATM exemption for venue purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action for infringement under section 281 of title 35, United States Code, of a covered business method patent, an automated teller machine shall not be deemed to be a regular and established place of business for purposes of section 1400(b) of title 28, United States Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory limitation on venue in covered business method patent suits: locations consisting solely of ATMs cannot create venue under 28 U.S.C. § 1400(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'covered business method patent'
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this section, the term 'covered business method patent' means a patent that claims a method or corresponding apparatus for performing data processing or other operations used in the practice, administration, or management of a financial product or service, except that the term does not include patents for technological inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive scope test: claims must be tied to performing data processing/operations used in practice/administration/management of financial products/services; explicitly excludes 'technological inventions.' The Director is authorized to issue regulations to determine whether a patent is for a technological invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director to issue regulations for 'technological invention' determination
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist in implementing the transitional proceeding authorized by this section, the Director shall issue regulations for determining whether a patent is for a technological invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative implementation note: USPTO/Director-level regulations will define the boundary between business-method patents and technological inventions for the transitional proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of construction regarding 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this section shall be construed as amending or interpreting categories of patent-eligible subject matter set forth under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the statutory provisions governing the transitional proceeding and definitions do not alter existing 35 U.S.C. § 101 jurisprudence or statutory categories of patent-eligible subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on issuance of patents — human organism (AIA § 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no patent may issue on a claim directed to or encompassing a human organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute statutory bar: claims directed to or encompassing a human organism may not result in the issuance of a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPEP / Patent laws index (topics referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page includes the MPEP index listing numerous patent-law topics and headings (examples: novelty; nonobviousness/obviousness; patentability conditions under 35 U.S.C. 101; claims (independent/dependent); written description/description of invention; enablement/what to contain; priority/filing date; reexamination; inter partes review; post-grant review; infringement; damages; venue; appeals; assignments; fees; patent term adjustment/extension; design and plant patents; secrecy orders; confidentiality; provisional applications; international applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This index entry is a pointer to substantive rules and standards located elsewhere in the MPEP and statutory/regulatory texts. For concrete criteria (e.g., novelty, nonobviousness, enablement, written description, claim drafting rules), consult the referenced MPEP sections and the cited statutory provisions.
